summary:
[  edit  ]
The Limit  SOP  creates geometry from samples fed to it by  CHOPs . It creates geometry at every point in the sample. Different types of geometry can be created using the Output Type parameter on the  Channels Page .

parameters.name: chanrx
parameters.description: Channels used to specify the rotational data of the geomtery created at each point. Only used when Output Type is " Polygon  at Each  Point " or " Primitive  Circle at Each  Point ".

parameters.name: chanry
parameters.description: Channels used to specify the rotational data of the geomtery created at each point. Only used when Output Type is " Polygon  at Each  Point " or " Primitive  Circle at Each  Point ".

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.name: output
parameters.description: ⊞  - The type of geometry the Limit  SOP  produces from its sample data.

parameters.label: Polygonal Line
parameters.name: line
parameters.description: Creates a point for each sample and connects them with a polygonal line.

parameters.label: Polygon  at Each  Point
parameters.name: polys
parameters.description: Places a polygon at each sample point. Number of points in polygon defined by Divisions.

parameters.description: Places a primitive circle at each sample point.

parameters.name: polyspheres
parameters.description: Places a polygonal sphere at each sample point. Sphere's frequency defined by Divisions.

parameters.label: Tubes

parameters.description: Creates a tube down the path. Tubes cross-section defined by Divisions.

parameters.label: Strips
parameters.name: strips
parameters.description: Creates a strip down the path. Number of points in strip defined by Divisions.

parameters.label: Divisions
parameters.name: divisions

parameters.label: Poly Sphere at Each Point

parameters.label: Tubes

parameters.label: Strips

parameters.label: Radius

parameters.label: Smooth Flip
parameters.name: flipsmooth
parameters.description: Dynamically controls the twist of each instance of geometry on a series of points to avoid frame-by-frame flipping, which can sometimes occur when geometry is oriented along a path.

parameters.description: Bounding region off.

parameters.label: Clamp
parameters.name: clamp

parameters.label: Loop

parameters.label: Zigzag

parameters.label: Y Limit

parameters.label: Z Limit
parameters.name: zlimit

parameters.label: Apply Texture
parameters.name: texture
parameters.description: Applys u, v, and w texture coordinates to the created geometry.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: texscale
parameters.description: ⊞  - Scales the texture coordinates a specific amount.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.name: texoffset
parameters.description: ⊞  - Offsets the texture coordinates a specific amount.

parameters.label: Orient to  Path
parameters.name: orient
parameters.description: If this option is selected, the object will be oriented along the path. To see what the path looks like, change the Output Type to "Polygonal Line". When the Output Type is " Polygon / Primitive  Circle at Each  Point ", the positive Z axis of each object will be pointing down the path. When the Output Type is "Tubes/Strips" then the cross-section of the geometry created will be pointing down the path.

parameters.label: Lookat  Object
parameters.name: lookat
parameters.description: Orient to  Path  must be checked for Lookat Object to have any effect. This allows you to orient your geometry by naming the object you would like it to Look At, or point to. Once you have designated this object to look at, it will continue to face that object, even if you move it. The Look At parameter points the each piece of geometry at the other object's origin individually.

parameters.label: Rotate Polys
parameters.name: dorotate
parameters.description: ⊞  - Rotate the geometry at each point using the Rotate parameter (below). Only works for Output Type is " Polygon / Primitive  Circle at Each  Point ".

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Do not rotate polys. Rotate parameter is greyed out.

parameters.label: On
parameters.name: on
parameters.description: Add value of Rotate to polys equally.

parameters.label: Cumulative
parameters.name: cum
parameters.description: Add value of Rotate to polys cumulatively (ie. increasing with each poly).

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.name: rotate
parameters.description: ⊞  - Rotation channels rx, ry, and rz for Rotate Polys parameter.

parameters.label: Compute Normals
parameters.name: normals
parameters.description: Computes normals for the geometry created.

parameters.label: num_points
parameters.description: Number of points in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_prims
parameters.description: Number of primitives in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_particles
parameters.description: Number of particles in this  SOP .

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: last_meta_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating meta surface geometry data (such as metaballs or nurbs) on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: total_cooks

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

POPs vs. SOPs - **Execution**: POPs run on the GPU (parallelized compute shaders); SOPs run on the CPU. - **Workflow**: POPs combine strengths of SOPs, CHOPs, and TOPs for a modern approach. - **Attributes**: POPs offer advanced attribute manipulation (e.g., multi-component, high precision). - **Limitations**: POPs lack some SOP features (e.g., tracing, booleans), though these may be added later. ## 4.
